# Volume 2 — XX The Way It Often Happens

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Nell got up early the following morning and cheerfully welcomed the new day, as the sunrise unfurled its banners victoriously over the pearl-colored skies. Grey Shutters rested in a sunlit pool, dappled with the moving shadows of willow and poplar. Past the property sat Mr. Pettifer’s wheatfield, a vast, breeze-rippled sheet of light gold. The world possessed such beauty that Nell passed ten joyful minutes leaning lazily across the garden gate taking the charm in.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0000 }

When breakfast was finished, Thirza prepared to set out on her trip. Lucy, who had been promised this enjoyment for a long time, was scheduled to accompany her.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0001 }

“Now, Robin, you attempt to be a well-behaved boy and do not annoy Nell,” she strictly instructed him. “If you behave yourself I will get you a striped candy cane from town.”
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0002 }

For regrettably, Thirza had lowered herself to the wicked practice of paying off individuals so that they would behave well!
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0003 }

“I won’t be bad intentionally, but what if I’m bad accidentally?” Robin wished to learn.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0004 }

“You must be careful to avoid mishaps,” cautioned Thirza. “Nell, should Mr. Shearer arrive today, purchase a good roast and a portion of steak. Should he fail to appear, you will need to butcher a bird for tomorrow’s midday meal.”
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0005 }

Nell gave a nod.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0006 }

“For simply Robin and me today, I won't trouble myself to cook dinner,” she said. “For lunch at noon, that cold ham bone is enough, and once you return home in the evening, I'll fry up some steak for you.”
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0007 }

“This morning, I am going to assist Mr. Pettifer in hauling dulse,” declared Robin. “Since he invited me, I expect he will also invite me for dinner. A terribly good man is Mr. Pettifer. He is a truly friendly man. When I am older, I hope to resemble him. That is, act as he does . . . I have no desire to resemble his appearance. However, I suppose that is unlikely, because according to Mrs. Sowerby, I am a quite good-looking youngster. Nell, do you think it will remain that way? I am curious to know?”
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0008 }

“I believe it certainly shall,” Nell remarked solemnly. “Robin, you are an attractive young man,” . . . Thirza’s expression conveyed deep disapprobation . . . “however, you have to match that appearance by acting every bit as polite and well-mannered as you seem.”
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0009 }

“And the other day, when Posy Fay Pembroke was crying because somebody called her ugly, you informed her that people wouldn't care about her appearance if she was loving and kind and nice,” Robin remarked unhappily. “It appears to me that, for one reason or another, you simply cannot escape being good in this world. You are forced to behave.”
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0010 }

“Do you not wish to be good?” questioned Thirza, a person who had acquired much knowledge but had still to understand how useless it was to ask these things.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0011 }

“Indeed, my desire is to be good, though not excessively so,” Robin remarked with care. “A person isn't required to be particularly good in order to serve as a Sunday School superintendent. Mr. Bell holds that position, and he is truly a wicked man.”
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0012 }

“Most certainly he isn’t,” Marila stated with indignation.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0013 }

“He is . . . he claims he is himself,” Robin declared. “During his prayer in Sunday School last Sunday, he uttered it. He declared that he was a vile worm, a miserable sinner, and responsible for the blackest ‘niquity. What was the terrible thing he did, Thirza? Did he murder someone? Or did he take the collection pennies? I want to know.”
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0014 }

By good fortune, Mrs. Sowerby drove up the lane just then, prompting Thirza to depart with a sense of having fled the fowler's trap, while earnestly hoping that Mr. Bell would use fewer elaborate figures of speech during his public prayers, particularly when listened to by young boys who were constantly “wanting to know.”
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0015 }

Nell, who had been left alone in her glory, set to work with a will. She swept the floor, made the beds, fed the hens, and washed the muslin dress before hanging it out on the line. After that, Nell made preparations to transfer the feathers. Going up to the garret, she put on the first old dress she happened to find . . . a navy blue cashmere that she used to wear when she was fourteen. It was certainly rather short and just as “skimpy” as the famous wincey Nell had been wearing when she made her debut at Grey Shutters; however, it would not suffer any significant harm from down and feathers. Nell finished dressing by tying over her head a large red and white spotted handkerchief that had once been owned by Obed, and, outfitted in this manner, she went to the kitchen chamber, where Thirza had assisted her in carrying the feather bed prior to her departure.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0016 }

Beside the room's window hung a mirror with a crack, and Nell happened to glance inside it at an unfortunate time. Positioned on her nose were those seven freckles, appearing to be even more prominent than before, or at least that was how they looked under the bright illumination streaming from the bare window.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0017 }

“Oh, I omitted applying that lotion yesterday evening,” it occurred to her. “I ought to hurry to the pantry to put it on right away.”
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0018 }

Nell had undergone numerous ordeals in her efforts to erase those spots. At one point, her nose lost its outer layer of skin entirely, yet the freckles persisted. Only a couple of days before, a magazine provided her with a formula for a freckle-clearing wash, and because the components were accessible to her, she mixed it up immediately, deeply offending Thirza, who believed that if Providence saw fit to put freckles on a person's nose, that person was obligated to keep them there.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0019 }

Nell hurried down into the pantry, a room that was perpetually shaded by the large willow tree near the window and had now become nearly pitch-black because the blind was lowered to keep out flies. Grabbing the bottle of lotion off the shelf, Nell generously slathered her nose using a tiny sponge reserved exclusively for that task. Having completed this essential chore, she went back to her labor. Anyone who has undertaken the transfer of feathers between ticks does not require an explanation to understand the spectacle Nell presented upon finishing. Down and fluff turned her dress white, while the front of her hair, which had slipped out from beneath her handkerchief, was decorated with a true ring of feathers. It was during this favorable instance that a knock rang out at the kitchen door.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0020 }

“Mr. Shearer must be here,” Nell reflected. “My appearance is terribly untidy, yet I must rush downstairs just like this because he is perpetually rushing.”
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0021 }

Down to the kitchen door flew Nell. Should a merciful floor ever split apart to consume an unhappy, plumage-covered maiden, the porch floor of Grey Shutters ought to have swallowed Nell immediately at that instance. Standing upon the doorstep were Honora Hollis, radiant and blonde in silk clothing, a brief, heavy-set, silver-haired woman wearing a tweed suit, and one more woman, lofty, majestic, extraordinarily dressed, possessing a lovely, refined visage and big, dark-lashed violet eyes, who Nell “instinctively felt,” as she might have expressed it during her younger years, was Mrs. Charlotte E. Varley.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0022 }

Amid the horror of that instance, a single idea emerged clearly from the turmoil of Nell’s thoughts, and she clutched it like the legendary straw. Every heroine created by Mrs. Varley was famous for “rising to the occasion.” Regardless of their misfortunes, they always rose to the occasion, proving themselves above every hardship of time, space, and quantity. Consequently, Nell believed she had an obligation to rise to the occasion, and she accomplished this so flawlessly that Honora later stated she had never held Nell Harcourt in higher esteem than at that instant. Whatever her offended emotions might have been, she hid them completely. She welcomed Honora and was presented to her friends with as much composure and calmness as though she were dressed in purple and fine linen. Granted, discovering that the woman she had intuitively assumed to be Mrs. Varley was actually a stranger named Mrs. Pendexter, whereas the plump, small, gray-haired lady was Mrs. Varley, came as a bit of a surprise; yet within the larger distress, this smaller one lost its effect. Nell led her visitors to the guest bedroom and then into the parlor, leaving them there while she hurried outside to assist Honora in unharnessing her horse.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0023 }

“I am sorry to drop in on you so suddenly,” Honora offered as an excuse, “however, it was only yesterday evening that I learned about our trip. Aunt Charlotte leaves on Monday, and she had agreed to pass this day alongside a city friend. Yesterday evening, though, this friend called her on the phone to cancel the visit since scarlet fever had put them under quarantine. Consequently, I proposed that we travel to this place, as I was aware of how much you wished to visit her. After stopping by the Pale Sands Hotel, we picked up Mrs. Pendexter to join us. Being an acquaintance of aunt’s, she resides in New York, and a millionaire is her husband. Our visit must be brief, because Mrs. Pendexter needs to return to the hotel before five o’clock.”
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0024 }

Nell noticed Honora glancing at her secretly and with confusion on multiple occasions as they were stabling the horse.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0025 }

“There is no reason for her to gaze at me in that manner,” Nell reflected with a slight touch of indignation. “If she lacks firsthand knowledge of turning a feather bed, she could at least picture what it entails.”
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0026 }

After Honora had departed for the parlor, and prior to Nell's ability to flee to the upper floor, Isolde stepped into the kitchen. Grabbing her arm, Nell held her startled friend.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0027 }

“Isolde Pembroke, who do you imagine is occupying that parlor right now? Mrs. Charlotte E. Varley . . . alongside the wife of a New York millionaire . . . while I am in this state . . . and there is nothing at all to serve for dinner except a cold ham bone, Isolde!”
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0028 }

At this point Nell realized that Isolde was gazing at her with the exact same confused expression that Honora had shown. It truly exceeded all limits.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0029 }

“Oh, Isolde, do not regard me in that manner,” she begged. “It ought to be clear to you, above everyone else, that even the most meticulous individual could not transfer feathers between two ticks and stay tidy throughout.”
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0030 }

“It . . . it . . . is not the feathers,” Isolde paused. “It’s . . . it’s . . . your nose, Nell.”
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0031 }

“My nose? Oh, Isolde, certainly there is nothing amiss with it!”
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0032 }

Nell hurried toward the small mirror above the sink. A single look confirmed the disastrous reality. Her nose shone a bright red!
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0033 }

Nell took a seat upon the sofa, her brave heart finally humbled.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0034 }

“What is the problem with it?” Isolde inquired, her inquisitiveness surpassing her sense of propriety.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0035 }

“I believed I was applying my freckle lotion to it, but I must have chosen that red dye Thirza uses to trace the pattern on her rugs,” came the hopeless reply. “What am I to do?”
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0036 }

“Rinse it away,” Isolde stated in a matter-of-fact tone.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0037 }

“Maybe it will not wash away. Initially I color my hair; after that I color my nose. Thirza sheared my hair away when I colored it but that cure would scarcely be feasible regarding this situation. Ah well, this serves as an additional penalty for vanity and I imagine I merit it . . . even if there is little solace in that thought. It actually is nearly sufficient to render a person a believer in bad luck, even though Mrs. Sowerby claims no such phenomenon exists, since all things are preordained.”
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0038 }

Lucky for her, the dye was removed without difficulty, and Nell, feeling a bit better, retreated to the east gable as Isolde hurried back to her house. Shortly after, Nell returned downstairs, dressed and restored to her senses. Because the muslin dress she had eagerly anticipated wearing was dancing cheerfully on the outdoor clothesline, she had no choice but to settle for her black lawn instead. She had already started the fire and set the tea to steep by the time Isolde came back; the second girl was actually wearing her muslin, and she held a dish with a lid in her hand.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0039 }

“Your mother has provided this for you,” she stated, raising the lid and exposing a beautifully carved and jointed chicken to the appreciative eyes of Nell.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0040 }

To the chicken were added fresh, light bread, fine butter and cheese, fruit cake from Thirza, and a bowl of preserved plums submerged in golden syrup that resembled solidified summer sun. A large basin filled with pink-and-white asters served as an ornament; nevertheless, the meal appeared quite scant when compared to the lavish feast previously made for Mrs. Varley.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0041 }

The famished visitors of Nell, nevertheless, appeared to find nothing missing and consumed the basic food with clear pleasure. Yet following the initial moments, Nell ceased considering what her menu did or did not contain. The look of Mrs. Varley could perhaps be rather unsatisfactory, a fact her faithful admirers had been compelled to concede to one another; however, she turned out to be a charming talker. Having journeyed widely, she was a superb raconteur. She had observed many men and women, condensing her observations into humorous short statements and adages that made her audience feel like they were hearing a character from smart literature. Yet beneath her entire radiance existed a deeply perceived baseline of genuine, feminine empathy and benevolence that captured love just as effortlessly as her genius captured esteem. Furthermore, she did not dominate the talk. She possessed the skill to elicit responses from others as adeptly and completely as she was able to speak herself, leading Nell and Isolde to discover that they were conversing with her without restraint. Mrs. Pendexter spoke minimally; she simply offered smiles with her beautiful eyes and lips, and consumed chicken, fruit cake, and preserves with a grace so refined that she gave off the sense of feasting on ambrosia and honeydew. Nevertheless, as Nell remarked to Isolde afterward, a person as heavenly gorgeous as Mrs. Pendexter was not required to speak; existing solely to be looked at was sufficient for her.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0042 }

Following dinner, the entire group took a stroll along Linger Lane, Primrose Dell, and the Aspen Path, before returning by way of the Whispering Wood to the Nymph’s Well, at which spot they seated themselves and conversed for an enchanting final thirty minutes. Mrs. Varley inquired about the origin of the Whispering Wood's name, and she wept with laughter upon listening to the tale and Nell’s theatrical description of a particular unforgettable walk taken through it during the magical time of dusk.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0043 }

“It certainly was an intellectual feast and a soulful exchange, wasn’t it?” Nell remarked once her visitors had left and only she and Isolde remained behind. “I’m unsure what gave me greater pleasure . . . hearing Mrs. Varley speak or looking at Mrs. Pendexter. My feeling is that our time was even more delightful than if their arrival had been anticipated and we had been burdened with preparing a great meal. You have to remain for tea with me, Isolde, so that we can discuss everything.”
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0044 }

“Honora says that an English earl is married to the sister of Mrs. Pendexter’s husband; and she nevertheless had a second portion of the plum preserves,” Isolde said, as though those two statements were somehow contradictory.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0045 }

“I reckon that Thirza’s plum preserves wouldn't have been sneezed at even by the English earl himself,” Nell stated with pride.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0046 }

That evening, as Nell recounted the events of the day to Thirza, she omitted the calamity that had happened to her nose. She did, however, grab the bottle containing freckle lotion and pour its contents out the window.
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0047 }

“I am never going to attempt any beautifying messes again,” she stated, with grim determination. “They might work for people who are cautious and deliberate; however, for someone as completely prone to making errors as I appear to be, it is inviting trouble to mess with them.”
{: #nw-v02-c20-p0048 }
